open_points.subject: Request validation order across operations
open_points.text: A01 rule 5: "This check comes before every other check of the request." vs A16 rule 1: "A request is handled in this order... size... token... operation/schema... actor... then the operation's own checks".
open_points.question: When a request includes a slot/flow purpose mismatch, must the kernel check and refuse that before token/schema/authorization checks, or only inside operation-specific checks after A16's global gate?
options: A01 is absolute: purpose check runs before all other request checks
A16 is absolute: purpose check runs only after size/token/schema/authorization
A01 priority applies only within operation-specific checks, not global surface checks
open_points.default_guess: A16 global order first; apply A01 'before every other check' only within that operation's own checks.

open_points.subject: `stored_value_bytes_max` measurement and `many` values
open_points.text: A12 rule 1: "each value... is within `stored_value_bytes_max`; for a `many` port, is a JSON array whose every element fits it"; A04 rule 1 and A15 rule 4 also enforce `stored_value_bytes_max` but do not define the byte representation for size checks.
open_points.question: What exact bytes are measured for `stored_value_bytes_max` (raw incoming bytes, canonical JSON bytes, or another form), and for `many` values is the limit applied to the whole array value, each element, or both?
options: Measure canonical JSON UTF-8 bytes of the whole value only
Measure raw request payload bytes as received
Measure both whole array and each element separately
open_points.default_guess: Measure canonical JSON UTF-8 bytes of the whole value; for `many`, apply limit to the array as one value.

open_points.subject: Ordering when `map_index` is absent in tuple order
open_points.text: A15 rule 1: "Records of nodes that become non-executable together are written in (`node_id`, `map_index`) order."
open_points.question: How is ordering defined when some records have no `map_index` (unmapped/aggregate records) and others have numeric indices?
options: Treat absent `map_index` as sorting after all numeric indices
Disallow mixed ordering cases by separate passes
open_points.default_guess: Treat absent `map_index` as before 0, matching A14 rule 2's explicit ordering style.

open_points.subject: Invocation-time stale-binding checks boundary
open_points.text: A08 rule 6: "fails one of rule 5's checks of the record itself — not those of the instance, which are A09 rule 6's own".
open_points.question: Exactly which rule-5 checks are considered "record itself" versus "instance" at send time, especially for failures that involve both manifest content and installation-selected instance data?
options: Only service file + capability-entry structure/name/effect/exposure/idempotency syntax are 'record itself'
Any check that reads selected instance fields counts as 'instance'
Use proposal-time order literally and map each check ad hoc
open_points.default_guess: Classify checks that depend on selected instance fields (`api_base_url`, required headers, instance presence) as A09 instance checks; all other manifest-entry checks as A08 record checks.
